key_idea: Best case for the runner-up is that every eliminated candidate's ballots all transfer to him, so just simulate eliminations from the smallest upward.
sketch: Sort the counts; if the leader already has a strict majority (2F > T) answer IMPOSSIBLE. Otherwise eliminate the remaining candidates in increasing order, adding each one's votes to the runner-up, and print the first round count where 2S > T; if all others are gone and it is still not a strict majority (exact tie with the leader) it is IMPOSSIBLE. O(c log c), 64-bit sums. Caveat: this is the simple reading that matches all four samples; a literal reading where transfers are split to engineer ties among low candidates (eliminating several in one round) could give fewer rounds, e.g. 1 5 6 100 99, and that is not modelled here.
